verdicts.title: Convert parity skips to strict xfail and resolve the gpt2 gradient mismatch
verdicts.rationale:
The test-gap half is still exactly true in the current tree, but the issue's causal diagnosis of gpt2 is WRONG and its second acceptance criterion would cause harmful work.

STILL TRUE. `_GRAD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES = {gpt2, qwen3_next, deepseek_v4, gpt_oss}` at packages/opaque-patches/tests/transformers/models/test_parity.py:97-103; consumed as plain `pytest.skip` at :278-279 (test_backward_grads_parity) and :483-484 (test_vmap_grad_parity). The coverage guard `test_parity_families_covered` at :509-520 still subtracts only `_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES` (:82-84), so it cannot see the grad exemptions or the three-family `_STRICT_FORWARD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES` (:88-92). `supported_families()` returns 26 families (verified by running it). No delta commit touched test_parity.py's skip sets: `git log --oneline 4b13d82..12146ec4 -- .../test_parity.py` shows only 5f615565 (#879, sliding window) among parity changes. Note the issue's line refs (85-93, 269-270, 456-457, 482-490) have drifted.

WRONG — gpt2 has no gradient defect. I cleared the skip set via a pytest plugin and reran: gpt2 fails both `test_backward_grads_parity` (transformer.h.0.attn.c_attn.bias abs_err=1.93e-02) and `test_vmap_grad_parity` (abs_err=1.12e-02, rel_err=3.70e+01), reproducing the audit. But the cause is the harness, not the patch. Running `assert_parity_grad` directly on a tiny GPT-2 pair: with default config, ALL 28 parameters mismatch AND the two losses differ (4.198711 vs 4.208967); with `resid_pdrop=embd_pdrop=attn_pdrop=0.0` the losses are bit-identical and 0 of 28 parameters mismatch. `assert_parity_vmap_grad` likewise PASSES with dropout zeroed and fails (c_attn.bias abs_err=4.36e-03) with dropout 0.1. Root cause: `get_tiny_config_kwargs()` (_test_utils.py:14-27) sets no dropout keys, and `assert_parity_grad` (:461-482) / `assert_parity_vmap_grad` (:525-556) put both models in `.train()` and run them sequentially off the shared global RNG, so the two models draw different dropout masks. GPT-2 is the only registered family with nonzero default dropout (llama-shaped configs default attention_dropout=0.0). `packages/opaque-patches/src/.../models/gpt2.py:41-49` applies only batchify + kv_cache and disables all family shims (`*_replacement=None`), so there is no backward-graph change to fix. Acting on the current acceptance criterion would either burn effort hunting a non-existent gpt2 backward bug or de-register a family that is in fact bit-exact.

WIDER THAN STATED. With the skip set cleared, `test_vmap_grad_parity[gpt_oss]` and `test_vmap_grad_parity[deepseek_v4]` PASS (stale exemptions), while `test_backward_grads_parity` for both fails on a structural key mismatch: `missing={'model.layers.0.self_attn.sinks'}`. That is not 'unreliable gradient parity' — it is a live fidelity break (see finding: the family patch replaces sink-aware attention with the llama-shaped shim, dropping `s_aux` and freezing `sinks`). Converting that entry to a permanent strict xfail without fixing the shim would cement a real bug behind a green suite.
verdicts.corrected_title: Make grad-parity exemptions strict and visible, and fix the dropout non-determinism that fakes the gpt2 failure
verdicts.corrected_body:
Parent: #769

## Problem

The parity suite exempts families from gradient and vmap-grad parity with bare `pytest.skip`, and one of those exemptions is caused by the harness rather than by the patches.

**1. The exemptions are invisible and cannot rot-detect.** `_GRAD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES = {gpt2, qwen3_next, deepseek_v4, gpt_oss}` (`packages/opaque-patches/tests/transformers/models/test_parity.py:97-103`) is consumed as a plain `pytest.skip` at `:278-279` and `:483-484`. `_STRICT_FORWARD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES` (`:88-92`) exempts three more families from forward parity. The coverage guard `test_parity_families_covered` (`:509-520`) subtracts only `_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES` (`:82-84`), so neither exemption set is visible to it. Nothing reports when an exempt family starts passing.

**2. Two exemptions are already stale.** Clearing `_GRAD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES` and rerunning: `test_vmap_grad_parity[gpt_oss]` and `test_vmap_grad_parity[deepseek_v4]` PASS today.

**3. gpt2 is not a patch defect — the harness is non-deterministic under dropout.** `assert_parity_grad` (`_test_utils.py:461-482`) and `assert_parity_vmap_grad` (`:525-556`) put both models in `.train()` and run them sequentially off the shared global RNG, and `get_tiny_config_kwargs()` (`:14-27`) sets no dropout keys. GPT-2 is the only registered family whose config defaults to nonzero dropout (`resid_pdrop=embd_pdrop=attn_pdrop=0.1`), so the two models draw different dropout masks. Measured on a tiny GPT-2 pair: at the default dropout all 28 parameters mismatch and even the two losses differ (4.198711 vs 4.208967); with the three dropout probabilities set to 0.0, the losses are bit-identical, 0 of 28 gradients mismatch, and `assert_parity_vmap_grad` passes. `models/gpt2.py:41-49` applies only `batchify` + `kv_cache` and disables every family shim (`*_replacement=None`) — there is no altered backward graph.

**4. The deepseek_v4 / gpt_oss backward-grads exemption hides a real defect.** With the skip cleared, `test_backward_grads_parity` for both fails with `missing={'model.layers.0.self_attn.sinks'}` — the patched model produces no gradient for the attention-sink parameter at all. The exemption reason ("runtime compatibility shims change sink gradients") understates this: the shim removes the sink from the softmax. Tracked separately; this issue must not convert that entry to a permanent xfail before it is fixed.

## Impact

The grad-parity suite reports green while (a) it is silently non-deterministic for any family with dropout, (b) two exemptions no longer correspond to any failure, and (c) one exemption conceals a genuine fidelity break in the family a user would train. Because the exemptions are `skip`, the hole is permanent by construction. `test_vmap_grad_parity` is the DP-relevant lane — `vmap(grad(...))` is exactly how per-record gradients reach `clipped_grad`.

## Acceptance criteria

- `get_tiny_config_kwargs()` (or `_base_config_kwargs`) forces every dropout probability to 0 for every family, and/or both grad helpers reseed immediately before each model's forward, so the comparison is deterministic. A regression test asserts parity on a family with nonzero default dropout.
- `gpt2` is removed from `_GRAD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES` once dropout is pinned; it passes both grad-parity tests. It is NOT de-registered from `supported_families()` — it is bit-exact.
- `gpt_oss` and `deepseek_v4` are removed from the vmap-grad exemption (they pass today).
- Remaining exemptions become `pytest.param(family, marks=pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason=...))` with an issue reference in the reason, so a family that starts passing fails the suite.
- `test_parity_families_covered` asserts that every family in `_GRAD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES` and `_STRICT_FORWARD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES` is a registered family and carries a reason, so the exemption sets cannot silently accumulate.

Audit source: OPQ-339.

verdicts.title: Bound v_k as a function of mu so strong audits converge instead of raising
verdicts.rationale:
Still fully reproducible in the current tree, and I can now prove the invariant rather than only the symptom — plus the `needs-design` label is no longer justified.

STILL PRESENT. `_MAX_EXACT_RANKS = 2000` at packages/opaque-auditing/src/opaque/api/auditing/one_run/_gdp.py:41; `r_prime = min(r, _MAX_EXACT_RANKS)` / `n_trunc = r - r_prime  # truncated ranks use v_k = 0.5` at :336-338; `expected = float(np.sum(v_k)) + n_trunc * 0.5` at :389; the capped bracket loop and raise at :79-92. Reproduced against the shipped surface with a synthetic `OneRunEstimate` (n_in=n_out=5000): `estimate.epsilon_at(delta=1e-5, threshold=0.5)` with (r=10000, u=3800) raises after 103.9 s — `cannot invert μ-GDP p-value for (m=10000, r=10000, u=3800) at significance=0.05: p-value stays below it for every μ up to 1.0289e+19` — while (r=10000, u=3900) returns ε=11.5598 in 16.1 s. So the cliff sits at ~62% attack accuracy at the guide's own m=10000.

NEW EVIDENCE — it is not slow convergence, the statistic is μ-blind. Calling `_p_value(10000, 10000, 3800, mu, 10000)` directly gives 4.5211e-05 at μ=10, μ=100, μ=1e4 AND μ=1e12 — identical to six significant figures over twelve orders of magnitude. Once u is below the pinned floor `n_trunc*0.5 = 4000`, μ carries no information at all, so no bracket width can ever succeed.

CORRECTIONS. (a) The raise is now `opaque.exceptions.OperationError` (subclasses RuntimeError) after 7b26f655 (#760), not a bare `RuntimeError`. (b) Line refs drifted (:40 -> :41, 80-91 -> :79-92, 331-334 -> :336-338, 384 -> :389). (c) #829's grid work (3ccf15ba, #890) raised `_MIN_GRID_SIZE` from 16 to 1000 (`_estimate.py:44, 192-195`) and changed nothing here — the truncation is orthogonal to grid resolution, as the μ-sweep above shows at the default grid of 10000. (d) The docs are still silent: `grep -n '2000|_MAX_EXACT|truncat' docs/user-guide/auditing.md docs/reference/auditing.md` returns nothing, while `docs/user-guide/auditing.md:220-228` still tabulates 10^4/10^5/10^6 canaries and says the ceiling "does not apply to the μ-GDP estimator".

TRACTABILITY — drop `needs-design`. `_compute_v_k` (:342-379) builds one `(r_prime, grid_size)` log-integrand and reduces with `logsumexp(axis=1)`; every row is an independent integral, so chunking over ranks computes all `r` values exactly at the same ~160 MB peak the 2000-rank cap was chosen for. That removes the defect with no new mathematics. Honest cost: runtime is linear in `r_prime`, so an exact r=10000 p-value costs ~6 s instead of ~1.2 s and a full bisection ~10 min, which is why a μ-decaying bound on the truncated tail is still worth having as the fast path. Either way this is an engineering task with a known-correct fallback, not an open research question.
verdicts.corrected_title: Stop the mu-GDP estimator from refusing strong audits: compute v_k for all ranks (chunked) or bound the truncated tail
verdicts.corrected_body:
Parent: #773

## Problem

`_MAX_EXACT_RANKS = 2000` (`packages/opaque-auditing/src/opaque/api/auditing/one_run/_gdp.py:41`) pins every rank past the top 2000 at `v_k = 0.5` (`:336-338`), so the Chernoff expectation has a hard floor of `n_trunc * 0.5` (`:389`). Once the observed error count `u` falls below that floor, **the p-value stops depending on μ at all** — `_p_value(m=10000, r=10000, u=3800, μ, grid=10000)` returns 4.5211e-05 at μ=10, μ=100, μ=10⁴ and μ=10¹², identical to six significant figures. The bracket search at `:79-92` therefore cannot succeed for any finite μ and raises `OperationError` after exhausting 60 doublings.

Measured on the default `epsilon_at` surface with n_in=n_out=5000:

| (r, u) | attack accuracy | result |
|---|---|---|
| (10000, 3900) | 61% | ε = 11.5598 in 16.1 s |
| (10000, 3800) | 62% | `OperationError` after 103.9 s |

The cliff is at roughly 62% attack accuracy at m = 10 000 — the scale `docs/user-guide/auditing.md:220-228` recommends, on a page that explicitly tells the reader its ceiling table "does not apply to the μ-GDP estimator". Neither auditing doc page mentions 2000, truncation, or any limit (`grep` over both returns nothing).

## Impact

The estimator fails exactly where it is most informative: the stronger the attack, the more likely the refusal. A practitioner following the guide's own canary-count advice on an under-noised mechanism gets an exception after ~100 s instead of the large ε the run actually demonstrates. It is fail-closed (no wrong ε is emitted), but the audit cannot do its job and nothing warns the user in advance.

## Acceptance criteria

- The default `epsilon_at` surface returns a finite ε for (m=10000, r=10000, u=3800), i.e. the p-value becomes a strictly increasing function of μ again for every reachable (r, u). Two acceptable routes, not mutually exclusive:
  - **Exact, no new mathematics:** chunk `_compute_v_k` (`:342-379`) over `k_vals` and compute all `r` ranks. Each row of the log-integrand is an independent integral, so chunking is exact and keeps peak memory at the current ~160 MB. Runtime is linear in the rank count (~5× at r=10000), so pair it with a cheaper fast path.
  - **μ-dependent bound:** any valid upper bound on `v_k` for truncated ranks that decays with μ restores p-value growth; state and cite the bound.
- A regression test pins the μ-monotonicity property directly (`_p_value` strictly increasing in μ at fixed (m, r, u) in the truncated regime), not just the absence of an exception.
- If any truncation survives, `docs/user-guide/auditing.md` states the limit next to the canary-count table, and the error message points at it.
- Remove the `needs-design` label: the chunked-exact route is a known-correct implementation task.

Statistical calibration under the null remains tracked by open #376.

verdicts.title: Sweep C — verify every citation against its record and its hypotheses
verdicts.rationale:
All six sites are still present in the current tree — nothing in the 124-commit delta or the #844 sweep touched any of them — but the issue bundles two kinds of work that have different owners, different evidence standards and different done-conditions, and two of its six factual claims need correcting. Splitting is the right move.

STILL PRESENT, verified site by site:
- OPQ-371: `packages/opaque-optimizers/src/opaque/api/optimizers/_schedule_free.py:10-11` still reads `Defazio, Yaida, Cutkosky, "The Road Less Scheduled", arXiv:2405.15682`. "Yaida" is not an author of that paper.
- OPQ-372: `packages/opaque-alignment/src/opaque/api/alignment/dpo/loss/_discopop.py:5-7` still attributes DiscoPOP to "Azar, M. G., et al. (2024) ... Using Self-Supervised Feedback" (Azar is the IPO author; DiscoPOP is Lu et al., arXiv:2406.08414). `logprob/_sequence.py:15-16` still says the `ld_alpha` split "is not implemented here; pass ``ld_alpha=None``" while the same file implements it at `:37, 54-62, 82-95`.
- OPQ-373: `packages/opaque-accounting/src/amplification/truncated_poisson.rs:18` and `:124` still cite the bare key `\[Gan25\]`; a repo-wide grep for `Ganesh` or `2508.15089` finds no definition anywhere (only unrelated Dong & Ganesh b-min-sep hits). `docs/reference/accounting.md:242-259` still describes the truncated form only as "not ... better than plain Poisson" and never says the guarantee is conditioned on a public, fixed `dataset_size`. 3b22a6af (#850) touched the file without adding the citation.
- OPQ-374: `docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/lambda-cgd.md:70-73` still says "The sensitivity formula (Theorem 1, eq 15 of the paper)", and `matrix_factorization/lambda_cgd.rs:8, 65, 130` repeats it — while the default path is `normalized=True` (`noise/_lambda_cgd.py:106, 175-176`) and its own Rust implementation documents a different result: `lambda_cgd.rs:154-161` says the normalized Gram comes "from Lemma 8 of the paper". So the docs attribute the deployed default to a theorem the code itself does not use.
- OPQ-375: `dpftrl/sampling/_balls_in_bins.py:3-5, 10, 27, 48` still cites "Definition 3.1"/"Lemma 3.2" of "Choquette-Choo et al. (2024), 'Privacy Amplification for Matrix Mechanisms'" with no arXiv id, next to a URL for Chua et al. arXiv:2412.16802.
- OPQ-376: `dpftrl/noise/_bisr.py:232-241` still hard-codes α=1 ("For alpha=1: c_k = ...") and `BisrStrategy` (`:629-688`) exposes no α.

TWO CLAIMS NEED CORRECTING.
(1) OPQ-375's premise is half wrong, and I verified it against the papers. Definition 3.1 (balls-in-bins batching) and Lemma 3.2 (Dimension-reduction for balls-in-bins batching) DO exist — in Choquette-Choo, Ganesh, Haque, Steinke, Thakurta, "Near Exact Privacy Amplification for Matrix Mechanisms", arXiv:2410.06266, pp. 7-8. The defect is that the sampler module cites them under the title of a DIFFERENT paper ("Privacy Amplification for Matrix Mechanisms", Choquette-Choo et al. 2024b, ICLR, whose corresponding result is Lemma 4.5) while the accounting module (`accounting/dpftrl/amplification/_balls_in_bins.py:47-48`) and the Rust side (`matrix_factorization/mod.rs:41`) use the correct title and id. So it is a wrong-title/missing-id defect, not an unfindable-result defect.
(2) OPQ-376's "enforces none of its 0 ≤ β < α ≤ 1 hypothesis" is now stale: e87a0c21 (#857) added `if not math.isfinite(self.momentum) or not 0.0 <= self.momentum < 1.0` at `_bisr.py:660-663`. With α pinned to 1 that is exactly β ∈ [0, α). What survives is the un-exposed α and the unvalidated `inv_coefficients` override (`:643, 674-688`), which lets a caller supply any C⁻¹ with no check against the lemma.

NEW, SAME SITE. `accounting/dpftrl/amplification/_balls_in_bins.py:3-4` states the dataset is "randomly partitioned into ``num_bins`` **equally-sized** bins", directly contradicting both its own sampler (`sampling/_balls_in_bins.py:4-6`: "Bin sizes are therefore **random**, following Binomial(N, 1/num_bins)") and Definition 3.1 of the cited paper. Which model holds is exactly what the dominating-pair argument depends on, so this belongs in the hypothesis half.

WHY SPLIT. OPQ-371, 372 and the bibliographic half of 375 are mechanical: wrong author, wrong title, missing identifier, docstring contradicting its own function. They can be closed by a generated per-file checklist and are verifiable by a reviewer with a browser. OPQ-373, 374, the equal-bins contradiction and the residual of 376 require reading theorem hypotheses against the deployed default configuration and then either constraining the code or writing down the assumption — DP review work under `.junie/differential-privacy-review.md`, on a different timescale, and OPQ-373 in particular carries an adjacency question (`dataset_size` public and fixed) that touches what the library is allowed to compose. Keeping them in one issue means the cheap half blocks behind the expensive half, which is what has happened for two audit cycles.
verdicts.corrected_title: Sweep C1 — make every citation resolve to the right record
verdicts.corrected_body:
Parent: #775

## Problem

Three citation sites still name the wrong record. Closed #418 swept the references once and missed `_schedule_free.py`; #503 re-introduced entries #502 had just deleted. A manual pass demonstrably does not hold.

| ID | Site | Defect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OPQ-371 | `opaque-optimizers/src/opaque/api/optimizers/_schedule_free.py:10-11` | Cites "The Road Less Scheduled" (arXiv:2405.15682) as "Defazio, Yaida, Cutkosky"; Yaida is not an author. Still unfixed from July's OPQ-136. |
| OPQ-372 | `opaque-alignment/src/opaque/api/alignment/dpo/loss/_discopop.py:5-7`; `logprob/_sequence.py:15-16` | DiscoPOP attributed to "Azar, M. G., et al. (2024) ... Using Self-Supervised Feedback"; the real record is Lu et al., "Discovering Preference Optimization Algorithms with and for Large Language Models", arXiv:2406.08414. Separately, `_sequence.py:15-16` states the `ld_alpha` (LD-DPO) split "is not implemented here" while the same module implements it at `:37, 54-62, 82-95`. |
| OPQ-375 (bibliographic half) | `opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/sampling/_balls_in_bins.py:3-5, 10, 27, 48` | Cites "Definition 3.1" and "Lemma 3.2" of "Choquette-Choo et al. (2024), *Privacy Amplification for Matrix Mechanisms*" with no identifier. Those results are in a **different** paper: Choquette-Choo, Ganesh, Haque, Steinke, Thakurta, *Near Exact Privacy Amplification for Matrix Mechanisms*, arXiv:2410.06266 (Definition 3.1 p. 7, Lemma 3.2 p. 8). The accounting module (`accounting/dpftrl/amplification/_balls_in_bins.py:47-48`) and `matrix_factorization/mod.rs:41` already use the correct title/id, so the tree is internally inconsistent. |

## Impact

A reviewer checking a sensitivity or amplification claim is sent to a paper that does not contain the cited result, or to no resolvable record at all. Two of the three are on privacy-relevant paths. The `_sequence.py` docstring additionally tells a user a shipped feature does not exist.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every citation in the three sites above resolves to a real record with correct authors, title and a stable identifier (arXiv id or DOI).
- `_sequence.py`'s module docstring describes the `ld_alpha` support the module actually implements, and names the fused path that does not support it (`:134`).
- The check is a per-file checklist generated from the source (every docstring/comment reference paired with an identifier) rather than a manual pass, so it survives the next refactor.

## Split out

OPQ-373, OPQ-374, the residual of OPQ-376, and a newly found contradiction at the OPQ-375 site are **hypothesis** defects, not bibliographic ones — the citation resolves but the result does not cover the deployed configuration. They need a mathematical answer, not a reference fix, and are moved to a sibling issue:

> **Sweep C2 — check every cited hypothesis against the deployed default** (parent #775)
>
> **Problem.**
> - **OPQ-373** — `opaque-accounting/src/amplification/truncated_poisson.rs:18, 124` cites the bare key `[Gan25]`; nothing in the repository defines it (the source is Ganesh, *Tighter Privacy Analysis for Truncated Poisson Sampling*, arXiv:2508.15089). That paper's guarantee is stated for a restricted add-or-remove-1-of-n adjacency with |D| fixed and public, and cautions against composing the result with other mechanisms. `p_trunc = Pr[Binom(n-1,q) >= B]` makes the analysis n-specific, yet `docs/reference/accounting.md:242-259` describes the truncated form only as "not better than plain Poisson" and the accountant composes it freely.
> - **OPQ-374** — `docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/lambda-cgd.md:70-73` and `matrix_factorization/lambda_cgd.rs:8, 65, 130` attribute the sensitivity to "Theorem 1, eq 15", but the default is `normalized=True` (`dpftrl/noise/_lambda_cgd.py:106, 175-176`) and the Rust normalized path documents a different result — "the Gram matrix from Lemma 8 of the paper" (`lambda_cgd.rs:154-161`). The docs cite a theorem the deployed default does not use, and eq (15) is a utility metric.
> - **OPQ-375 (hypothesis half)** — `accounting/dpftrl/amplification/_balls_in_bins.py:3-4` says the dataset is "randomly partitioned into `num_bins` **equally-sized** bins", contradicting its own sampler (`sampling/_balls_in_bins.py:4-6`: sizes are Binomial(N, 1/num_bins)) and Definition 3.1 of arXiv:2410.06266. Which participation model holds is what the dominating pair depends on. (The signed-encoder hypothesis of Lemma 3.2 — C lower-triangular with non-negative entries — was already addressed by e87a0c21 / #857 via the |C| triangle-inequality extension; document that as the assumption it is.)
> - **OPQ-376 (residual)** — `dpftrl/noise/_bisr.py:232-241` implements Lemma 1 with α hard-pinned to 1 and exposes no α on `BisrStrategy` (`:629-688`). The β half of the `0 <= β < α <= 1` hypothesis IS now enforced (`:660-663`, added by #857), so only the un-exposed α and the unvalidated `inv_coefficients` override (`:643, 674-688`) remain: a caller-supplied C⁻¹ is checked for length, finiteness and leading magnitude, but never against the lemma's hypotheses.
>
> **Acceptance criteria.** For each site, the cited result's hypotheses are written out and checked against the deployed default; any gap is closed in code (a validation) or stated as an assumption in the user-facing docs; `[Gan25]` is replaced with the full citation; the truncated-Poisson docstring and `docs/reference/accounting.md` state that the guarantee is under add-or-remove-1-of-n with `dataset_size` public and fixed, that this is a different adjacency from plain Poisson, and that the source cautions against composing it; the λ-CGD docs cite the result the normalized default actually uses; the balls-in-bins bin-size description is made consistent across sampler, accountant and paper.
>
> Audit source: OPQ-373, 374, 375, 376.

Audit source: OPQ-371, 372, 375.

findings.title: Patching gpt_oss / deepseek_v4 silently deletes the attention sink and freezes the `sinks` parameter
findings.claim: `make_apply_family_patches` defaults `eager_attention_replacement=vmap_eager_attention_forward` (`transformers/_family.py:126, 212-215`), and neither `models/gpt_oss.py:16-19` nor `models/deepseek_v4.py:16-20` overrides it. Both upstream families compute attention with an extra sink logit — `sinks = module.sinks.reshape(1,-1,1,1)...; combined_logits = torch.cat([attn_weights, sinks], dim=-1)` (transformers `modeling_gpt_oss.py:251-252`, `modeling_deepseek_v4.py:724-725`) and pass `s_aux=self.sinks` into the attention interface (`modeling_gpt_oss.py:329`, `modeling_deepseek_v4.py:849`). Opaque's replacement takes `**kwargs` (`attention.py:373`), swallowing `s_aux`, and delegates to `_grouped_eager_attention`, a plain llama-shaped softmax with no sink term. Both families declare `_supports_sdpa = False` (`modeling_gpt_oss.py:387`, `modeling_deepseek_v4.py:1171`), so the module-global `eager_attention_forward` the patch rebinds is the only path a non-flash run can take.
findings.failure_scenario: Fine-tune a GPT-OSS or DeepSeek-V4 checkpoint with DPTrainer or any `apply_model_patches(model)` flow. Verified on a tiny GptOssForCausalLM with DEFAULT kwargs (no `eager_attention=True` needed): after `apply_model_patches(m2)`, `transformers.models.gpt_oss.modeling_gpt_oss.eager_attention_forward` is `vmap_eager_attention_forward`, forward logits shift by 1.54e-01 max abs versus the unpatched model, and after a backward pass `model.layers[0].self_attn.sinks.grad is None` — the attention-sink parameter receives no gradient and never trains. The parity suite cannot catch this: `gpt_oss` and `deepseek_v4` are in `_STRICT_FORWARD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES` (test_parity.py:88-92) so forward parity is skipped, and in `_GRAD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES` (:97-103) so grad parity is skipped; clearing the latter makes `test_backward_grads_parity` fail immediately with `missing={'model.layers.0.self_attn.sinks'}`. Privacy is unaffected (clipping still bounds per-record sensitivity), but the model being trained is not the model the user loaded, and `docs/user-guide/huggingface/model-patches.md:215-218` states the opposite: for GPT-OSS and DeepSeek-V4 "only RMSNorm, RoPE (where standard), and cross-entropy are patched".
evidence: packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/components/attention.py:365-387 — signature ends in `**kwargs`; body calls `_grouped_eager_attention(module, query, key, value, attention_mask, scaling, dropout)`; no `s_aux` / sink term anywhere in packages/opaque-patches/src (grep for `sinks` returns zero hits)

Reproduction (uv run python, tiny GptOssForCausalLM, default `apply_model_patches(m2)`): `after default apply: vmap_eager_attention_forward` / `default-apply max logit diff: 0.1544521450996399` / `sinks grad after default apply: None`

Parity run with `_GRAD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES` cleared: `AssertionError: gpt_oss gradient key mismatch: extra=set(), missing={'model.layers.0.self_attn.sinks'}` and the identical failure for deepseek_v4
docs/user-guide/huggingface/model-patches.md:215-218 claims only RMSNorm/RoPE/CE are patched for these two families
findings.fix_sketch: Either pass `eager_attention_replacement=None` for gpt_oss and deepseek_v4 (as gpt2 already does, `models/gpt2.py:35`) so upstream attention is left alone, or add a sink-aware vmap shim that forwards `s_aux` into the softmax the way `modeling_gpt_oss.eager_attention_forward` does. Then remove both families from `_STRICT_FORWARD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES` and `_GRAD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES` so forward and gradient parity actually guard them. Until fixed, the doc table must not claim attention is unpatched for these families.

findings.title: Grad-parity harness is non-deterministic under dropout and mis-attributes the failure to the patches
findings.claim: `assert_parity_grad` and `assert_parity_vmap_grad` put both the unpatched reference and the patched model into `.train()` and run them one after the other off the shared global torch RNG, and `get_tiny_config_kwargs()` sets no dropout keys. Any family whose config defaults to nonzero dropout therefore draws different dropout masks in the two runs, and the helper reports the difference as a patch-parity failure. GPT-2 is the only currently registered such family, which is why the suite's `_GRAD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES` entry for gpt2 carries the (incorrect) reason "kv_cache/batchify patches alter backward graph".
findings.failure_scenario: Running `assert_parity_grad(GPT2LMHeadModel, GPT2Config, cpu, config_kwargs=<tiny>)` with GPT-2's default `resid_pdrop=embd_pdrop=attn_pdrop=0.1` mismatches ALL 28 parameters and even the two losses (4.198710918 vs 4.208966732). Setting the three probabilities to 0.0 in the same call makes the losses bit-identical and 0 of 28 gradients mismatch; `assert_parity_vmap_grad` likewise fails (c_attn.bias abs_err=4.36e-03) at dropout 0.1 and passes at dropout 0.0. The consequence is twofold: a real family was written off as having broken gradients when it is bit-exact, and any newly registered family with default dropout (or any future config default change upstream) will produce the same false failure, which the suite's existing habit is to resolve by adding another name to the skip set.
evidence: packages/opaque-patches/tests/transformers/models/_test_utils.py:14-27 — `get_tiny_config_kwargs()` returns vocab/hidden/layers/heads/rope only; no dropout keys
_test_utils.py:461-482 — both models `.train()`, `loss_ref = unpatched(...)`; `loss_ref.backward()`; then the patched forward/backward, with no reseed between them
_test_utils.py:525-556 — `assert_parity_vmap_grad` has the same structure via `_vmap_grads(unpatched)` then `_vmap_grads(patched)`

Measured: dropout 0.1 -> 28/28 parameters mismatch and losses differ; dropout 0.0 -> `n mismatch 0 of 28` and losses identical. vmap variant: `drop=0.1: FAIL -> gpt2 drop=0.1: vmap_grad transformer.h.0.attn.c_attn.bias mismatch: abs_err=4.36e-03`, `drop=0.0: VMAP GRAD PARITY PASSES`

packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/models/gpt2.py:32-49 — family shims all disabled (`repeat_kv_replacement=None`, `eager_attention_replacement=None`, `rope_replacement=None`); only batchify + kv_cache apply
packages/opaque-patches/tests/transformers/models/test_parity.py:97-99 — the skip entry and its incorrect reason
findings.fix_sketch: Force every dropout probability to 0 in `get_tiny_config_kwargs()` / `_base_config_kwargs()` (or call `torch.manual_seed(seed)` immediately before each of the two forward passes in both grad helpers), then drop gpt2 from `_GRAD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES`. Add one regression case that runs grad parity on a family with nonzero default dropout so the determinism is pinned rather than accidental.
